issues.legal_issue: A co-owner may use jointly owned land and a common channel for irrigation from an exclusive well unless that use prejudicially affects or detrimentally burdens another co-owner.
material_facts: The parties admitted their co-ownership of the land and channel in which the common well was situated.
One side used a small channel across the common land to carry water from its exclusive well to its own fields.
The opposing co-owners objected but did not plead or prove damage, injury, hardship, or other prejudice from that use.
The lower courts found the use advantageous to the users and modified the decree to address possible prejudice.
issues.conclusion: The users were entitled to use the common land and channel to carry water from their exclusive well, and the opposing co-owners could not prevent that use in the absence of pleaded or proved prejudice or detriment.
issues.legal_principle: A co-owner's rights comprise a bundle of rights that includes use of the common property, subject to the limitation that the use must not prejudicially affect or put another co-owner to a detriment. Findings must be made with reference to the specific pleadings. The Court approved the reasoning in Subbiah Goundan v. Ramaswamy Goundan, AIR 1973 Mad. 42, and distinguished Sivarama Pillai v. Marichami Pillai, AIR 1971 Mad. 230, which concerned agreed terms governing use of a common well.

rule.if: co_ownership_use_dispute and shared_land_or_channel and exclusive_source_used_for_irrigation and not prejudice_pleaded_or_proved

predicates.co_ownership_use_dispute: The proceeding concerns a dispute over one co-owner's use of jointly owned property.
predicates.shared_land_or_channel: The property used to convey water is held in common by the disputing co-owners.
predicates.exclusive_source_used_for_irrigation: A co-owner conveys water from a source under that co-owner's exclusive control across the common property to irrigate land.
predicates.prejudice_pleaded_or_proved: Another co-owner specifically alleges or establishes that the use prejudicially affects or detrimentally burdens that co-owner.

issues.definition: When a co-owner uses common land or a channel to irrigate from an exclusive water source, and no other co-owner pleads or proves prejudice, the co-owner may use the shared property for irrigation.

issues.legal_issue: The statutory illustration concerning a co-owner imposing an easement does not govern a claim founded primarily on co-ownership rights.
material_facts: The claim to use the common land and channel was based primarily on admitted co-ownership.
The claim of an easement was advanced only as an alternative ground.
The High Court relied on the illustration concerning a co-owner imposing an easement.
issues.conclusion: The illustration did not apply because the principal claim rested on co-ownership, not on an easementary right.
issues.legal_principle: Section 8, illustration (c), of the Indian Easements Act applies when a co-owner seeks to impose an easement on the land or a part of it; it does not govern a claim whose main basis is the claimant's right as a co-owner.

predicates.co_ownership_claim_proceeding: The proceeding concerns a claim to use property held in common.
predicates.claim_based_primarily_on_co_ownership: The claimant principally relies on rights arising from co-ownership rather than on an easement.
predicates.easement_claim_only_alternative: The claimant raises an easement only as an alternative basis for the requested use.

issues.definition: If a claimant principally seeks use of common property as a co-owner and relies on an easement only alternatively, the illustration about imposing an easement does not apply.

issues.legal_issue: A judge should not decide contrary to an applicable decision of the same High Court without referring the matter to a larger bench.
material_facts: A party cited an earlier decision of the same High Court concerning a similar use of a common channel.
The High Court judge decided contrary to that decision without referring the matter to a larger bench.
issues.conclusion: The judge should have followed the earlier decision or referred the matter to a larger bench; judicial propriety did not warrant deciding contrary to it.
issues.legal_principle: Judicial propriety and decorum require a judge of a High Court not to hold contrary to a decision of that same court; a judge who disagrees should refer the issue to a larger bench. The Court approved Subbiah Goundan v. Ramaswamy Goundan, AIR 1973 Mad. 42.

predicates.intra_court_precedent_issue: The proceeding raises whether a judge was bound by an earlier decision of the same court.
predicates.lower_court_judge_disagrees_with_same_co: A judge decides contrary to an applicable decision of the same court.
predicates.no_larger_bench_reference: The judge does not refer the disagreement to a larger bench.

issues.definition: When a judge disagrees with an applicable decision of the same court and makes no larger-bench reference, the judge must follow that decision or refer the issue to a larger bench.

issues.legal_issue: An agreed arrangement governing the use of common irrigation property controls, but an unstipulated limitation cannot be inferred merely because a co-owner uses an exclusive water source or irrigates additional land.
material_facts: The common well and channel had been kept for the parties' common enjoyment at partition.
There was no stipulation governing the manner or mode of enjoyment of the common well or channel.

The water was taken from a well on land exclusively belonging to the users, and the opposing co-owners argued that use of the channel would impose an additional burden and that newly acquired land could not be irrigated through it.
The decision relied on in support of that argument concerned a partition arrangement that expressly fixed the manner and duration of use.
issues.conclusion: Any contract governing use would control, but there was no such stipulation here; neither law nor expediency justified preventing irrigation through the common channel from the exclusive well.
issues.legal_principle: The terms of an agreement governing common property control the parties' use of it. Sivarama Pillai v. Marichami Pillai, AIR 1971 Mad. 230, was distinguishable because the parties there had agreed on a mode and duration of use at partition; no comparable term existed here.

rule.if: common_property_use_proceeding and partition_created_shared_irrigation_property and no_agreed_mode_of_use and exclusive_source_used_for_irrigation

predicates.common_property_use_proceeding: The proceeding concerns the use of jointly held property for irrigation.
predicates.partition_created_shared_irrigation_prop: A partition left an irrigation source or conveyance property in common for the parties' enjoyment.
predicates.no_agreed_mode_of_use: The parties did not stipulate how or when the common irrigation property could be used.
predicates.exclusive_source_used_for_irrigation: A co-owner conveys water from a source under that co-owner's exclusive control through the common property for irrigation.

issues.definition: Where partition leaves irrigation property in common without specifying a mode of use, a co-owner's use of it to convey water from an exclusive source cannot be barred merely because that use is said to be unintended or an additional burden.
